thread:
rachel: heads-up — noticed OTLP exporter throughput spikes on Dedicated when routing attr churns per-request. memory climbs and exporter fanout multiplies resources. anyone seen this?
jason: yep saw that on canary yesterday, looked like new Resource per unique `routing.route_id` is causing exporter to open many streams.
marta: is the route set as a resource attr or just a span attribute in your test?
rachel: resource attr. quick snippet from service: ```python
# called per request
span.set_attribute('redwood.routing.route_id', route_id)
resource = Resource.create({'service.name': 'inference', 'tenant.id': tenant})
tracer.start_as_current_span('rpc', resource=resource)
```
jason: aha. when resource keys change we create new Resource -> exporter treats as different series. OTLP exporter (our fanout) keeps per-resource buffers which explodes.
arjun: the root cause is high-cardinality resource attr tied to routing decisions. retention+ingest cost will spike too.
marta: can we debounce route attr inside SDK so we only emit a new resource if route_id is stable for, say, 1s? That gives us per-session semantics without per-request churn.
rachel: that was my thought. alternative: keep route as span attribute (not resource) so telemetry ties to a trace but exporter uses stable resource keys. tradeoffs?
jason: span attr solves exporter buffering but harder to query in console grouping by resource. console dashboards are mostly resource-based for availability metrics.
arjun: consider hybrid: Normalise route -> compute `route_bucket` (hash(windowed)) and only change resource when bucket flips. Debounce window configurable per-sdk.
marta: also think about sampling earlier: per-tenant sampler in SDK can drop noisy tenant traces before export. both reduce costs.
rachel: agree. actionable: prototype debounce+bucket in python sdk and a matching minimal change in go. if prototype looks ok we port to rust.
jason: small prototype note: avoid locking hot path. debounce should be lock-free: e.g. use atomic last-emitted + timestamp compare. pseudo: ```go
if atomic.LoadUint64(&lastEmitTS) + window < now { emitResource() }
```
arjun: add tests for metric: unique resource count per hour under load. we need a dashboard query to alert if unique_resource_count/hour > threshold.
marta: also flag to console: surface 'approximate routing cardinality' to product so teams know when their routing patterns are telemetry-costly.
rachel: i'll open GH issues: one for python debounce + sampler hook, one for go prototype, one for dashboard query + alert, and one for console UX to show routing cardinality.
devops-bot: Deploy pipeline: canary job queued for eng-runtime svc — tag=canary-telemetry-test.
jason: quick Q — will debounce obscure useful short-lived route transitions we want to debug?
marta: group that under: enable debug-mode in SDK to bypass debounce and emit all changes. keep it opt-in.
arjun: also ensure exporter handshake/backpressure still works when we drop resource changes — don't leak buffers. add e2e with OTLP ingester sim.
rachel: perfect. Thanks all. I'll post links once issues up. :+1:
